newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen surge due to fall in Tokyo stocks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen surge due to fall in Tokyo stocks.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen futures contract surged on Friday, due to a sharp fall in Tokyo share prices.
The weakness of the stock market led to thinking in the market that interest rate levels will have to remain low, traders said.
"Due to such views, short-covering demand was stronger than expected," a trader for a brokerage house said.
The September confirmed a solid bottom after making a try for the downside the previous day, and this was another reason for its firmness on Friday, the trader said.
Demand for the September remained strong at below 99.15, a trust bank trader said.
The September moved within a range of 99.18 to 99.24 during the day. Turnover was 76,333 contracts.
In the Tokyo stock market, the Nikkei 225 average fell below the 20,000 level for the first time since September 3, jolted by the Dow's steep fall on Thursday of nearly 100 points.
The Nikkei 225 bounced back somewhat at the end of Friday's session to finish at 20,341, down 159.81 points from the previous day.
Earlier in the day there was some uncertainty in the market about the effect of the dive in Tokyo share prices.
"Weak stocks are theoretically positive for Euroyen, but if they drag down Japanese government bond futures too much, that would be another story," a city bank trader said.
In the afternoon, however, JGBs shook off some early depression with some "flight-to-quality" buying which benefited the shorter-end of the yield curve most, bond traders said.
The combination of weak share prices and firmness in JGBs is positive for Euroyen futures, another city bank trader said.
The weighted average of the overnight call rate is likely to be 0.47 percent on Friday, traders said.
The Bank of Japan injected 100 billion yen this morning, maintaining a neutral money market stance, on the last day of the current bank reserves reporting period.

The key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs), as well as two-month CDs, were tagged with a sell quote of 0.50 percent. About 10 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.50 percent.--Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk
